### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf), sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/capabilities/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/positions.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via sys_business_unit (literal, a string literal in headOf))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in managerOf))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 48 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e9a0461ad39c9e3d82aacd1d13c46e2f0622af5` — the merge of head `f357cc8f8fe25e9f7fc24e622331692b34c005c7` into base `946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e9a0461ad39c9e3d82aacd1d13c46e2f0622af5 && git checkout 5e9a0461ad39c9e3d82aacd1d13c46e2f0622af5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e f357cc8f8fe25e9f7fc24e622331692b34c005c7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e && git merge --no-ff f357cc8f8fe25e9f7fc24e622331692b34c005c7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 946a173fcbe44a7d6961656a47156322a6ae4b1e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f357cc8f8fe25e9f7fc24e622331692b34c005c7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/business-unit-head-manager-reads.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts (`readMembershipToCompletion`, `holderReadRefusal`, `managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg`, `TeamGraphService.managerOf`, `expandPrincipal`), packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts, packages/types/src/object-absence.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts (`IBusinessUnitGraphService`, `ITeamGraphService`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`lookupManager`, `expandBusinessUnitUsers`), the existing pins business-unit-graph.test.ts / manager-org-screen.test.ts / sharing-rule.test.ts, and the hotcrm and docs.objectos.ai trees (caller trace). The changeset is a prose face and is read for ②, not reviewed.

Face: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and on the changeset; `reviewFace` on the three paths with that declaration answers the narrowing face (no schema or governed `hits`). Net diff against the merge base `c76c0e04`: exactly the three files above; `team-graph.ts` and `packages/spec` are untouched. Predecessor PR #29703 (`48981622`) is an ancestor of this head, so the serial constraint holds.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `BusinessUnitGraphService.headOf`: a failed `sys_business_unit` read now throws `[sharing] the head of business unit 'ID' could not be read: REASON. …` instead of answering `null`. Judged RIGHT. In the tree the read goes through `readMembershipToCompletion`, which rethrows every non-absence error via `holderReadRefusal` with the driver error as `cause`; the `catch { row = null }` is gone.
2. `headOf` caches nothing after a failed read. Judged RIGHT. `this.cache.head!.set(businessUnitId, head)` is the first statement after the awaited read, so a throw leaves the map untouched; the cache key (the unit id), the `has()` short-circuit and the cached value (`string | null`, set only after a completed read) are byte-identical to `main` and the same shape as #29703's `descendants` cache (key = unit id, set only after `seedIsUsable` and the child walk complete).
3. `headOf` on absence: `readMembershipToCompletion` answers `null` on `isObjectAbsentError` (missing table, or `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` naming the read object), `rows?.[0]` is `undefined`, `head` is `null` and is cached — the same answer and the same caching `main` gave absence through its catch. Judged RIGHT. A unit that does not exist, sits in another organization (strict `orgScope`) or has no `manager_user_id` still answers `null`; the three existing `headOf` pins in `business-unit-graph.test.ts` and `sharing-rule.test.ts` that cover those cases are unchanged.
4. `headOf` projection and read count: `fields: ['manager_user_id']` becomes `['id', 'manager_user_id']` inside the helper, the projection `main` had. `keysetWalk` returns on a short page (an emitted page smaller than the page it asked for), so a one-row answer is still one read. Judged RIGHT; no accept-set change.
5. Standalone `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` (no `teamGraph`): a failed `sys_user` read throws `[sharing] the manager of user 'ID' could not be read: …`; absence answers `null`; a user with no `manager_id` answers `null`. Judged RIGHT. This limb has no cache on `main` or here, so the card's "and caches it" premise holds for `headOf` only — the dev's correction is confirmed from the `main` source.
6. The organization screen on the standalone limb is unchanged: `managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg` keeps its own `try/catch` that fails open on a failed `sys_member` read (ruled, #10153), so dropping the outer `try` around it changes nothing on that read. Judged RIGHT.
7. The wired limb `if (this.teamGraph) return this.teamGraph.managerOf(userId, organizationId)` is unchanged, and `team-graph.ts` is not in the diff. Judged RIGHT.
8. Module constant `SYSTEM_CTX` removed from `business-unit-graph.ts`: not exported, no reader left (the helper reads under `team-graph.ts`'s own `SYSTEM_CTX`, as `seedIsUsable`, `readChildUnits` and `readMembers` already did). Judged RIGHT; no public-surface change. The `memberScope` doc comment's `{@link SYSTEM_CTX}` becomes prose, so no dangling link.
9. Public surface: `IBusinessUnitGraphService` (`packages/spec`) is unchanged, `index.ts` exports are unchanged, no new export. The only observable narrowing is the failure posture of two methods on the exported class. Judged RIGHT.
10. Callers (traced in this tree, in hotcrm and in docs.objectos.ai): `headOf` has no production caller anywhere (tests only; hotcrm's `managerOf` hit is a local test variable). `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` has no production caller: `sharing-rule-service.ts` constructs the class and calls `expandUnitMembers` / `expandUsers` only; `ownership-queue-service.ts` likewise; `approval-service.ts` uses its own `lookupManager` and `expandBusinessUnitUsers` and never constructs the class; `expandPrincipal`'s `manager` arm calls `TeamGraphService.managerOf`, not this class. So no pass on `main` can newly fail where it used to drop one person. Judged RIGHT, and this is what makes the narrowing safe to ship with no caller change.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29713-business-unit-head-manager-reads-refuse.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `fix(plugin-sharing)!:` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Correct under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): a non-protocol narrowing with `none` ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner; both predecessors (#29606 `e0187d0f`, #29655 `48981622`) shipped the same shape at `patch`. The changeset's claims match the diff: it names both methods, says absence still answers `null`, says the wired limb is unchanged, and says no caller on this release changes behaviour (confirmed in ①.10). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right line: no accept set widens; a failure answer narrows from `null` to a refusal.

Check-runs on `f357cc8f` at the time of this record (read four times through the commits API, the last read governs): 23 completed success (Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label, Flag docs affected by code changes), 13 skipped by path filter, and 10 still in progress: Test Core shards 1 to 8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. No run is red. Those ten conclusions are the gate verdicts the landing check reads; this record judges the tree and does not pre-empt them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared. Nothing to answer.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; attribution comment names `os-warren`. No login note owed.
- Skills-docs `not needed`: confirmed. No `content/docs/**` page and no `skills/**` file names `headOf`, `managerOf`, `manager_user_id` or the standalone fallback, or states what either answers on a failed read.
- Premise correction (dev): "only `headOf` caches". Confirmed from `main`: `DeptCache` has a `head` map and no manager map; the standalone limb never wrote a cache. The card's wanted shape ("nothing is cached after a failed read") is still met for both, and the `managerOf` not-cached pin is a regression guard, as the dev says.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (dev, not filed): `TeamGraphService.managerOf` (`team-graph.ts`) catches a failed `sys_user` read to `null` and caches it under `org::userId` for the pass. Confirmed in the tree. Judged a FOLLOW-UP CARD, not this PR: the order and the claim's file surface kept the wired limb and `team-graph.ts` unchanged; it is a different class with its own organization-qualified cache and its own pins (`manager-org-screen.test.ts`); and its reach today is the exported `expandPrincipal` `manager` arm with no in-repo caller, so no grant on `main` is computed from it either. Same family, same grade (p3). ESCALATED here for the seat to file; see ④ S2.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (dev): the refusal sentence's consequence clause speaks of a "holder set" and an "expansion" for a single head or manager. Confirmed; belongs to `holderReadRefusal` in `team-graph.ts`, which has two arms (`expansion`, `check`) and neither fits a single lookup. Should-fix in the follow-up (④ S4), not a reason to hold this PR.
- `exceptions` (PR body folds the template; model-free co-author; `pnpm lint` run by order): none touches a review face.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`): `IBusinessUnitGraphService.headOf` is declared "Return the department head (manager_user_id) — best-effort, null when none", and `managerOf` "proxy to ITeamGraphService.managerOf", itself "best-effort; null when none". The declared capability is "the head, or `null` when the unit has none"; the PR keeps that at every consumer (no head, unknown unit, foreign-org unit, absent object all still answer `null`). What it takes away is an answer the spec never declared: `null` for a read that failed. "Best-effort" is prose on the lookup, not a declared accept set, and `expandUsers` / `descendants` on the same interface were given the same refusal by #29606 and #29655 without a spec change. So the narrowing does not remove a declared capability at the consumer; it makes the service consistent with its own sibling reads and with the spec's "null when none". The design holds.

Tried to break it:

- Cache after a failed read: the `set` sits after the awaited helper; the helper rethrows; nothing is written. The not-cached pin fails one read then expects the real head on the same instance, and the dev's A1/A2 ablations (catch-to-null put back; `null` pre-cached) each turn it red. Holds.
- Absence masking a real failure: `isObjectAbsentError` requires a missing-table error or `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` naming the read object itself; a `SQLITE_IOERR` is neither, and the pins run on a real SqlDriver with the table dropped versus the object never registered, so "absent" is what the driver says, not a double's guess. Holds.
- Pagination against `where: { id }`: `keysetWalk` ANDs the cursor with `$and` rather than overwriting the `id` equality, and returns on the short first page, so a unique-id lookup is one read with the same projection. Holds (and is the shape `seedIsUsable` already runs on `main`).
- The standalone limb's screen: the fail-open `sys_member` read keeps its own catch inside `managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg`; the removed outer `try` only ever covered the `sys_user` read and trivial string coercion. The screen's six existing pins in `manager-org-screen.test.ts` are unchanged. Holds.
- Pins cover each method's three cases: for `headOf` — refuses (named unit, `SQLITE_IOERR`), absence (object not registered; table dropped), not cached (fail once then real head on the same instance); for standalone `managerOf` — the same three with the user named; plus healthy controls (head / no head; manager / no manager) and a wired-limb control. Each negative pin was ablated red once (A1 to A3). Covered.
- Whole-pass failure: no production caller exists for either method (①.10), so no reconciler, approval or queue pass can newly throw where it used to drop one person. Holds.

Findings (none is a must-fix):

- S1 should-fix (spec prose, follow-up): the JSDoc "best-effort" on `IBusinessUnitGraphService.headOf` and `ITeamGraphService.managerOf` now describes one implementation that refuses and one that swallows. Align the two sentences to "refuses on a failed read; `null` when none" when the sibling is fixed — a `packages/spec` prose change that belongs with S2, not in this PR.
- S2 should-fix (follow-up card, p3): `TeamGraphService.managerOf` swallows a failed `sys_user` read to `null` and caches it for the pass; same class as this card and #29655. Reach today: `expandPrincipal` `manager` arm (exported, no in-repo caller) and the wired `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` limb. File it; it is the last read of this family in `plugin-sharing`.
- S3 should-fix (test, fold into S2): the CONTROL test hard-codes `expect(await failed.managerOf(ALICE, ORG)).toBeNull()` for the wired limb on a failed read. That line pins the sibling's swallow rather than the pass-through; the equality assertion beside it (`toBe(await new TeamGraphService(...).managerOf(...))`) is the control. The S2 fix will have to delete that one `toBeNull()`; nothing to change here.
- S4 should-fix (wording, fold into S2): `holderReadRefusal`'s consequence clause for a single head or manager lookup. A third arm (`lookup`) in the helper, not a local sentence.

**VERDICT: PASS**
